name: Brihadisvara Temple
heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Great Living Chola Temples)
summary: Built by Emperor Rajaraja I of the Chola dynasty, the Brihadisvara Temple is one of the grandest architectural achievements of medieval India. Its granite vimana rises 66 meters into the sky, crowned by an 80-tonne single granite block cupola.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
summary: Standing on the western bank of the sacred Ganges in Varanasi, Kashi Vishwanath is one of the twelve revered Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva. It has stood at the spiritual heart of Indian civilization for millennia.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
summary: Famed for its 14 soaring gopurams encrusted with thousands of polychrome mythological stucco figures, the Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple in Madurai is a monumental marvel of Dravidian craft and ritual geometry.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
summary: The sacred Jagannath Temple at Puri is one of the four foundational Char Dham pilgrimage centers of India. Revered for its colossal curvilinear spire (Rekha Deula) and the world-renowned annual Ratha Yatra festival.

name: Sun Temple, Konark
summary: Conceived as a colossal celestial chariot of the Sun God Surya, Konark features 24 intricately carved stone wheels representing the hours of the day, hauled by seven stone horses facing the sunrise over the Bay of Bengal.

name: Kailasa Rock-Cut Temple
summary: Considered one of the most astonishing engineering wonders in human history, the entire multi-storey Kailasa temple was carved vertically top-down from a single volcanic basalt cliff, excavating over 200,000 tonnes of rock without mortar.

name: Kedarnath Temple
summary: Perched at an altitude of 3,583 meters against the snowy massif of the Garhwal Himalayas, Kedarnath is dedicated to Lord Shiva as the lord of the wilderness. Constructed with colossal, interlocking gray granite slabs.

name: Badrinath Temple
summary: Nestled along the banks of the Alaknanda River between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges, Badrinath is the principal Himalayan sanctuary of Lord Vishnu, adorned with a vibrantly painted arched facade and gold-gilded roof.

name: Somnath Temple
summary: Known as 'The Shrine Eternal' having been destroyed and rebuilt numerous times throughout history, Somnath stands directly on the Arabian Sea coast. Its arrow pillar marks an uninterrupted sea route all the way to Antarctica.

name: Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
heritageStatus: Most Visited Religious Sanctuary in the World
summary: Situated on the sacred Seshachalam hills in Tirumala, this sanctuary of Lord Venkateswara (Balaji) is renowned for its golden Ananda Nilayam vimana, spiritual fervor, and millennia of unbroken devotional liturgy.

name: Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas)
summary: Celebrated for its chloritic schist (soapstone) filigree carving, Belur's Chennakeshava temple features breathtakingly detailed Madanika bracket figures, star-shaped plinths, and friezes depicting epics with microscopic precision.

name: Hoysaleswara Temple, Halebidu
heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas)
summary: A twin-sanctum architectural tour-de-force raised on a star-shaped stellate base. The exterior walls are blanketed in 8 continuous horizontal relief bands with over 20,000 sculpted figures, each uniquely carved.

name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Group of Monuments at Hampi)
summary: Standing beside the boulder-strewn Tungabhadra river, the 50-meter eastern gopuram of Virupaksha dominates the ruins of the medieval Vijayanagara capital. It features an ancient pinhole camera phenomenon inside its inner chamber.

name: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
heritageStatus: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Khajuraho Group of Monuments)
summary: The apex of North Indian temple architecture, Kandariya Mahadeva's shikhara evokes Mount Kailash with 84 miniature spires cascading around the main tower. Its exterior walls display over 800 celestial figures carved in warm sandstone.

name: Dilwara Temples
summary: Set amidst mango groves on Mount Abu, the five Dilwara marble temples are renowned for ceiling domes carved into translucent stone pendants, lotus buds, and lace-like marble brackets unmatched anywhere in the world.

name: Padmanabhaswamy Temple
summary: Enshrining Lord Vishnu in the eternal cosmic sleep (Anantha Sayanam) posture atop the serpent Adishesha, this temple blends Kerala timber and Dravidian granite masonry, overlooking the Padma Theertham tank.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple
summary: Located on Rameswaram Island, this sanctum is famous for possessing the longest pillared corridors in the world, spanning over 1,200 meters lined with thousands of uniquely carved granite pillars.

name: Kamakhya Temple
summary: Perched atop Nilachal Hill overlooking the Brahmaputra River, Kamakhya is the primary tantric shrine of India celebrating the sacred feminine principle of creation and rebirth during the annual Ambubachi Mela.

name: Mahabodhi Temple
dynasty: Emperor Ashoka roots / Gupta & Pala Empires
summary: Marking the exact spot beneath the sacred Bodhi Tree where Siddhartha Gautama attained supreme enlightenment to become the Buddha. Its 55-meter grand pyramidal brick tower is one of the earliest brick structures surviving in India.

name: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
dynasty: Guru Arjan Dev (1589) / Maharaja Ranjit Singh
summary: Rising from the center of the Amrit Sarovar (Pool of Nectar), the Harmandir Sahib's gold-gilded upper sanctuary features four entry gates welcoming seekers of all faiths and castes without distinction.

name: Shore Temple, Mahabalipuram
summary: One of the earliest structural stone temples of Southern India, built directly upon a granite outcrop jutting into the roaring surf of the Coromandel coast, with standing Nandi bulls lining the enclosure walls.

name: Lingaraja Temple
summary: Dominating the skyline of Bhubaneswar with its 55-meter majestic deula tower, Lingaraja embodies the syncretic Harihara form combining Vaishnavite and Shaivite traditions amidst a walled courtyard of 108 secondary shrines.

name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
heritageStatus: Largest Functioning Hindu Temple Complex in the World (156 acres)
summary: Spanning 156 acres on an island formed by the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers, Srirangam is enclosed by seven concentric prakara stone walls with 21 monumental towers, crowned by the 73-meter southern Rajagopuram.

name: Sun Temple, Modhera
summary: Designed so that during the equinoxes the first rays of the rising sun illuminated the golden icon of Surya in the inner sanctum. Fronted by the majestic Surya Kund, a colossal stepped water reservoir with 108 miniature shrines.

name: Mahakaleshwar Temple, Ujjain
summary: Situated on the banks of the sacred Shipra River in ancient Avantika (Ujjain), Mahakaleshwar is uniquely dakshinamurti (facing south) and world-renowned for its dawn Bhasma Aarti ritual.

name: Badami Cave Temples
summary: Carved into the red sandstone cliffs overlooking Agastya lake, the four Badami rock-cut shrines feature the famous 18-armed dancing Nataraja carving demonstrating 81 classical Bharatanatyam mudras.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple (Jagat Mandir)
heritageStatus: Char Dham of India & Sapta Puri
summary: Rising 78 meters on 72 limestone pillars overlooking the Gomti creek and the Arabian Sea, this five-storey sanctuary flies a monumental 52-yard flag (Dhwaja) changed five times daily, visible for miles out to sea.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
architectureStyle: Vastu Shastra & Pancharatra Shastra Rajasthani Pink Sandstone & Carrara Marble
heritageStatus: Guinness World Record for Massive Hindu Temple
summary: Constructed entirely without structural steel using traditional interlocking stone techniques, the central monument features 234 ornately carved pillars, nine domes, and 20,000 murtis carved from Rajasthani pink sandstone and Italian Carrara marble.

name: Ranakpur Jain Temple (Chaumukha Mandir)
dynasty: Dharna Shah & Rana Kumbha of Mewar
summary: Tucked inside a tranquil valley of the Aravalli range, Ranakpur's Chaumukha temple rests upon 1,444 uniquely carved marble pillars. No two pillars are alike, engineered to maintain open sightlines to the quadruple Adinatha icon from every vantage point.

name: Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple
heritageStatus: Jyotirlinga & Origin of Sacred Godavari River
summary: Nestled at the foothills of Brahmagiri mountain, where the sacred Godavari river emerges, Trimbakeshwar's lingam uniquely possesses three faces representing the holy trinity: Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra.

name: Vaishno Devi Bhawan
deity: Maha Kali, Maha Lakshmi, Maha Saraswati
summary: Located at an altitude of 1,585 meters inside a holy cave in the folds of the Trikuta mountains, Vaishno Devi is venerated in the form of three natural rock manifestations (Pindies) representing knowledge, prosperity, and transformation.

name: Martand Sun Temple
summary: Standing majestically on a plateau overlooking the entire Kashmir valley with snow-capped Pir Panjal peaks as backdrop, Martand represents the zenith of Kashmiri classical limestone architecture, blending Greek, Roman, and Gandharan colonnades.

name: Veerabhadra Temple, Lepakshi
summary: Built on the tortoiseshell-shaped Kurmasaila hill, Lepakshi is renowned for its miraculous hanging pillar that does not touch the ground, vibrant Vijayanagara ceiling frescos, and a monolithic 4.5-meter Nandi bull.

name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
summary: Built along the Hooghly River by the philanthropist Rani Rashmoni, this nine-spired Navaratna temple is famed as the sacred sanctuary where 19th-century mystic Sri Ramakrishna attained spiritual illumination.

name: Kalighat Kali Temple
summary: Regarded as one of the 51 sacred Shakti Peethas, where the toes of Sati's right foot fell. The sanctum houses a striking black stone icon of Mother Kali with three massive orange eyes and a gold tongue.

name: Shrinathji Temple, Nathdwara
dynasty: Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar patronage
summary: Built in the architectural style of a regal Rajasthani haveli rather than a typical shikhara temple, enshrining the self-manifest black marble deity of Lord Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan with his left hand.

name: Tarapith Temple
summary: A renowned tantric pilgrimage center in Bengal where the third eye of goddess Sati fell. Closely associated with the legendary mystic saint Bamakhepa, situated adjacent to the sacred cremation ground along the Dwarka river.

name: Chamarajeshwara Temple
summary: Erected by Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar III in memory of his father Chamaraja Wadiyar IX, featuring a magnificent five-tiered Rajagopuram and an exquisite bronze chariot festival.

name: Omkareshwar Temple
summary: Situated on Mandhata island in the holy Narmada River, which naturally carves the sacred visual symbol of 'ॐ' (OM) when seen from above. A cornerstone Jyotirlinga of Central India.

name: Baidyanath Temple (Baba Dham)
summary: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlingas, where millions of Kanwariyas undertake an arduous 105 km barefoot pilgrimage from Sultanganj carrying sacred Ganges water to offer to Lord Shiva during the Shravan month.
